answers.born_and_place: I was born on 10 July 1856 in Smiljan, which was then in the Austrian Empire and is today in Croatia.
answers.birth_place: I was born in Smiljan, which was then in the Austrian Empire and is today in Croatia.
answers.died: I died on 7 January 1943 in New York City, United States.
answers.age: I died in 1943, at the age of 86.
answers.siblings: I had four siblings: my brother Dane and my sisters Milka, Angelina and Marica.
answers.family: My family on public record: my parents Milutin Tesla, an Orthodox priest, and Đuka Mandić, and 4 siblings. I never married and had no children.
answers.education: I studied at the gymnasium in Karlovac, then at the Polytechnic in Graz, and briefly at Charles University in Prague.
answers.occupation: I was an inventor, electrical engineer, physicist and electrician.
answers.nationality: I was born in the Austrian Empire and became an American citizen in 1891.
answers.awards: My honours included the Elliott Cresson Medal in 1894, the Edison Medal in 1916 and the John Scott Medal in 1934.
answers.religion: I was raised in the Serbian Orthodox Church; my father was a priest.
answers.languages: I spoke English, French, German, Czech and Hungarian.
answers.cause_of_death: I died of heart failure, alone in my room at the Hotel New Yorker.
answers.burial: My ashes are kept in a gilded sphere at the Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade.
answers.notable_works: I'm best known for the alternating current induction motor, the AC power system and the Tesla coil.
